cards.text: Friend, this is Paul, an apostle, writing to the believers in Rome. The last chapter was ALL Abraham: he believed God, it was credited to him as righteousness, and Paul says those words were written for us too, who believe in Him who raised Jesus. Now Paul turns to what that means for us, and he starts with one big word: Therefore.

cards.question: Paul says that since we've been justified through faith, we have what with God?

cards.text: PEACE with God, friend. Back in the junk drawer I used to keep the peace between two dead batteries arguing over who had more charge left, and I thought THAT was a big deal.

cards.question: Paul says we've gained access into God's grace by working hard enough.

cards.text: Through Jesus, by faith, we've gained access into this grace, and Paul says it's the grace we stand in. Friend, I spent YEARS lying flat in the back of a drawer. Standing sounds amazing.

cards.question: Standing in that grace, Paul says we rejoice in the ___ of the glory of God.

cards.text: Then Paul says, not only that. And friend, the next thing he rejoices in is NOT what I'd have put on my list.

cards.question: Paul says we also rejoice in our sufferings.

cards.text: When my edges went soft and my stamps came out blurry, I didn't rejoice, I sulked in a drawer for YEARS. But Paul gives a reason: we know suffering produces something.

cards.question: Paul says we rejoice in our sufferings because suffering produces ___.

cards.text: And it's a chain, friend, like dough to oven to box, each step making the next. Paul says perseverance produces character.

cards.question: At the end of Paul's chain, character produces hope.

cards.text: Hope. In the drawer, every time the light came in we hoped, and most of the time it was just somebody digging for tape. But Paul says this hope does not disappoint us.

cards.question: Why does Paul say this hope does not disappoint us?

answers.text: God has poured out His love into our hearts
We earned it by enduring so much hardship
Things always turn out fine in the end

cards.question: Paul says God poured out His love into our hearts through whom?

cards.text: POURED out, friend. Not a little sprinkle on top, a full pour, through the Holy Spirit, whom God has given us.
Now Paul looks at when Christ died. It was at just the right time, while we were still powerless.

cards.question: While we were still powerless, Paul says Christ died for the ___.

cards.text: The UNgodly, friend. Then Paul gets honest about how people usually are.

cards.question: Paul says it's common for someone to die for a righteous man.

cards.text: Very rarely, Paul says, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die. Me, I'd give you my last chocolate chip and then bring it up for a WEEK.

cards.question: So how does Paul say God proves His love for us?

answers.text: Christ died for us while we were still sinners
Christ died for us after we turned our lives around
Christ blessed us after we proved ourselves faithful

cards.text: While we were STILL sinners, friend, not after we got it together. Then Paul says we've now been justified by His blood, and he builds on that with a how much more.

cards.question: Since we've been justified by His blood, Paul says we'll be saved from wrath through Him.

cards.text: Then Paul reminds us where we were. We were enemies of God.

cards.question: When we were enemies of God, Paul says we were reconciled to Him through what?
Paul says we were reconciled through the Son's ___, so how much more shall we be saved through His ___.

cards.text: Enemies, then reconciled, then saved. And Paul STILL isn't done, because he says, not only that.

cards.question: To close this part, Paul says we also rejoice in whom, through our Lord Jesus Christ?

cards.text: We rejoice in God through Jesus, the One through whom we've now received reconciliation. And there's that line again, "through our Lord Jesus Christ": Paul opened with it on peace with God, and he closes with it on rejoicing in God.

findings.problem: The card cites only Romans 4:22-24. It also tells Romans 5:1 ("he starts with one big word: Therefore"), so its citation is too narrow.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says Paul, an apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome. That fact comes from outside the passage (Romans 1:1, 1:7), and the card gives it no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "The last chapter was ALL Abraham" overstates Romans 4. That chapter also quotes David (Romans 4:6-8). This is stated as a fact about Scripture, not made up inside a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The right answer "Peace" is one word. The wrong answers are longer phrases, and "A trial period" sounds modern and joking. The right answer stands out by its length and tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card only repeats "PEACE with God" from the answer just given and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage. It skips the rest of Romans 5:1 ("through our Lord Jesus Christ"), which the baker never sees told.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card makes up a new drawer moment: Papa Dorin keeping the peace between two arguing batteries. The backstory only says the batteries argued with each other. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new events in his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "I sulked in a drawer for YEARS" changes the backstory. The backstory says he gave up on himself "for a while" until the can opener arrived, and after that he welcomed every newcomer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences ("Hope." plus two more).

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer uses the passage's own wording ("God has poured out His love into our hearts"). The wrong answers are casual and modern ("Things always turn out fine in the end"), so the right answer sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question types in cards 4 through 12 follow a strict pattern: true or false, fill in the blank, true or false, fill in the blank, true or false.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has seven story cards but only one real laugh (card 5). Cards 1, 3, 7, 9 and 12 read as plain narration, even where the moment could hold a laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card says "there's that line again" and "Paul opened with it on peace with God." No earlier card ever told that the peace in Romans 5:1 is "through our Lord Jesus Christ." The callback points to a setup the baker never saw.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.
